abstract: We present an overview of recent results obtained in pure and nano-dopant modified liquid crystals which possess extraordinarily ultrafast nonlinear nonlinearities for all-optical processing with lasers of wide ranging temporal and spectral characteristics.

articleTitle: Study of the impedance mismatch at the end-facet of a parallel plate waveguide operating in the THz regime
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We study the impedance mismatch for terahertz waves propagating in a parallel plate waveguide via the TEM mode. The impedance mismatch is found to be a strong function of the plate separation.

articleTitle: The transition from TEM-like mode to plasmonic mode in finite-width THz parallel-plate waveguide
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report the near-field measurement of the electric field distribution inside the metal PPWG. We observe the transition from TEM-like mode to plasmonic mode. This mode transition depends on the geometry of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Optimally chirped CARS spectroscopy using fiber stretchers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: High spectral resolution CARS spectroscopy is performed using a femtosecond laser system. By employing fiber stretchers for easy pulse delivery and for optimally chirping, the spectral resolution was improved by a factor >; 16.

articleTitle: High-speed THz biochip reader system
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A new all-electronic system is presented for THz biochip read-out. It is superior to common time-domain spectroscopy systems in terms of size, speed and costs. Exemplary biochip measurements are compared to TDS based read-out data.

articleTitle: Few-cycle CEP-stable source at 2.1 μm based on collinear OPA in BiB3O6
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a scalable, CEP stable, three-cycle source at 2.1 μm with 180 μJ pulse energy from OPA in bulk BiB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> at 3 kHz repetition rate without post-compression.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy with focused beams: Gouy shift correction for highly accurate refractive index retrieval
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Terahertz spectroscopic measurements are usually performed in focused beam geometry while the standard extraction procedure of the sample refractive index assumes plane-wave approximation. We demonstrate a new retrieval model for spatially limited Gaussian terahertz beams.

articleTitle: A high resolution, chirped pulse lidar for simultaneous range and velocity measurements
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A lidar based on the coherent detection of oppositely chirped optical pulses is used to perform range measurements with sub-millimeter resolution and simultaneous velocity measurements. A target moving at 212km/h is tracked with 20dB SNR.

articleTitle: Optical inspection of ITO conducting glass with optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A new approach for defect inspection and properties evaluation of indium t in oxide (ITO) conducting glass is demonstrated with optical coherence tomography (OCT). With OCT scanning, the defects can be clearly identified at the different depths. Besides the morphological information, several parameters also can be estimated including the thickness of glass, group refractive index, reflection coefficient and transmission coefficient, which can be used to evaluate the quality of ITO conducting glass. Fro m the results, one can see that OCT could be a potential imaging tool for defect inspection of ITO conducting glass or other industrial products.

articleTitle: Long tube precise THz-TDS measurement of the transmission of the atmosphere from 0.2 to 2 THz
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: In order to assess the potential of THz applications in imaging, sensing, ranging and communications, it is important to know the frequency dependent transmission of the atmosphere. Essentially, all of the attenuation of the atmosphere in the range from low frequencies up to 2 THz is caused by water vapor. Here we report the most accurate measurement of this attenuation to date.

articleTitle: Optical-parametric-amplification imaging of complex objects
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We used ultrafast Fourier-plane OPA imaging to image, wavelength-shift, and amplify complex two-dimensional objects with spatial features from 1.1 to 11.3-line pairs/mm, corresponding to a 2D space-bandwidth product (SBP) of 13,790.

articleTitle: Generation and verification of traveling-wave phase-sensitive eigenmodes of an optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We investigate the eigenmodes of a traveling-wave phase-sensitive optical parametric amplifier. We observe gain (deamplification) of 11.4 dB (-7.9 dB) for a Laguerre-Gaussian LG<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</sub> mode with >;95% overlap with the fundamental eigenmode.

articleTitle: 2D+3D face imaging for stand-off biometric identification
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We developed and tested a Fourier Transform Profilometry, 2D+3D face imager operating with subjects moving at ≤1.5 m/s at ≤25-m range with <;1.4-mm resolution and range precision at 1-Hz capture rate using low cost components.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral imaging technology and systems, exemplified by airborne real-time target detection
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging exploits the information contained in the spectrum of light, and has many applications. Systems require specialized cameras and application-specific image processing. As an example, we describe an airborne system with real-time image processing.

articleTitle: PMD mitigation in RZ-OOK PDM systems based on a single polarization-diversified all-optical regenerator
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: PMD mitigation in 2×10-Gb/s RZ-OOK PDM systems is demonstrated through a single all-optical-regenerator with polarization-diversified loop configuration. 3.0-dB eye-diagram-based SNR improvement is achieved in the presence of 6.3-ps DGD for RZ signals with 18-ps pulsewidth.

articleTitle: In vivo imaging using second-harmonic nanoparticles
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate second-harmonic nanoparticles as nanoprobes for long-term and in vivo imaging. The nanoparticles emitted a stable signal over five-hour continuous excitation and showed great contrast in a living mouse tail at 100 μm depth.

articleTitle: THz electro-absorption effect in quantum dots
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Instantaneous electro-absorption effect in quantum dots, induced by electric field of THz pulse with 3 THz bandwidth is demonstrated in THz pump — optical probe experiment. This effect may be promising for Tbit/s wireless transmission systems.

articleTitle: Measurement of wavefront distortions resulting from incidence of high-power 2 μm laser light
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Wavefront distortions induced in various silica samples by a 2 μm thulium fiber laser were measured. Absorption of silica at 2 μm makes a full characterization of thermal lensing critical for high power applications.

articleTitle: Finding decoherence free subspaces without process tomography
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Quantum process tomography (QPT) is a resource intensive task. We present an experiment in which a 3 dimensional decoherence free subspace is experimentally identified using 36 measurements, instead of the 256 measurements required for QPT.

articleTitle: IQE and EQE of the nitride-based UV/DUV LEDs
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Internal and external quantum efficiency and injection efficiency of nitride-based UV/DUV devices were investigated. Non radiative component in the photoluminescence and electroluminescence is found to be strongly correlated with the dislocation density.

articleTitle: High temporal contrast front end with a multipass Ti:Saamplifier and a CaF2-based XPW temporal filter
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A laser system applying spectrally shaped multipass amplifier and cross polarized wave generation produces pulses with 80 nm bandwidth at O.lmJ energy level, while the temporal contrast of the amplified 100 TW pulses exceeds 5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>.

articleTitle: Characterizing isolated atomic unit attosecond pulses
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Characterizing shorter attosecond pulses has been limited by an approximation in the FROG CRAB retrieval. We demonstrate a new technique based on interference in laser-assisted photoionization which can characterize ultrabroadband attosecond pulses.

articleTitle: Designing Bessel filters based on coupled-resonator optical waveguides for dispersion-free slow light
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We have developed a formalism for designing Bessel filters based on coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs). The CROWs feature maximally flat group delay and can be realized on different types of resonators.

articleTitle: Continuous-wave second harmonic generation of a tunable CO2 laser in orientation-patterned GaAs
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Frequency doubling of a tunable continuous wave CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser in orientation patterned GaAs is demonstrated. For 1.8 W incident power at 9.29 μm, 1.9 mW of second harmonic power was obtained from a 4 cm long crystal.

articleTitle: Generation of >100 μJ, broadband THz transients with >10 MV/cm fields via coherent transition radiation at the linac coherent light source
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Highly compressed, relativistic electron bunches are fired through a thin Be foil to generate intense, broadband, high-field THz transients. Pulse energies greater than 100 μJ and field strengths greater than 10 MV/cm are measured.

articleTitle: Molecular sensing with supercontinuum radiation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Supercontinuum radiation sources are becoming ubiquitous in a large range of scientific applications. They offer enormous spectral bandwidth and high brightness ideal attributes for applications in molecular sensing, improving both speed and sensitivity of detection. There are challenges too, however: supercontinuum generation is an inherently noisy process and some wavelength regions of interest for molecular sensing are as of yet difficult to reach. We review the current state-of-the-art of molecular sensing with supercontinuum radiation and reflect critically on current challenges and future opportunities.

articleTitle: Energy exchange between two filaments in air via a traveling plasma grating
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We observe efficient energy exchange between filaments in air mediated by a travelling plasma grating formed at the intersection of the two filaments. The velocity of this grating is studied by means of Doppler effect.

articleTitle: Light shifts of ground-state quantum beats: A monitor of quantum jumps
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Two-mode cavity QED allows the observation of ground-state quantum Zeeman beats with the conditional measurement of the intensity. Continuous π excitation produces quantum jumps that cause light shifts and induce decoherence.

articleTitle: Light extraction methods in light-emitting diodes
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: This paper describes the basics of light extraction in light-emitting diodes covering the ways light is trapped, is lost, and escapes. Additionally, methods to maximize light extraction in various UV-visible emitting semiconductors are shown.

articleTitle: Ultracompact surface plasmon polariton unidirectional generator based on asymmetric single-nanoslit
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: An asymmetric single-nanoslit with lateral dimension of only 370 nm is demonstrated to work as an efficient SPP unidirectional generator at wavelength of 830 nm.

articleTitle: Grating coupler integrated photodiodes for plasmon resonance based sensing in fluidic systems
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate an integrated sensor combining a grating-coupled plasmon resonance surface with a planar photodiode. Plasmon enhanced transmission is employed as a sensitive refractive index (RI) sensing mechanism and monitored via the integrated photodiode.

articleTitle: In vivo two-photon imaging of cortical vasculature in mice to 1.5-mm depth with 1280-nm excitation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Deep tissue multiphoton imaging of mouse brain using 1280-nm excitation is presented. A record imaging depth of 1.5-mm in mouse cortex is achieved in vivo, approximately reaching the fundamental depth limit in scattering tissue.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared absorption microscopy with λ/100 spatial resolution using tunable quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Highly-sensitive mid-infrared microscopy is reported. Subwavelength resolution is achieved by detecting absorption through local sample expansion. High sensitivity is obtained by moving laser pulses repetition rate in resonance with the atomic force microscope cantilever eigenfrequency.

articleTitle: Direct comparison of high-order harmonics generated in gas and in carbon plasma
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We perform the first direct comparison between high-order harmonics generated from carbon plasma and from argon gas cell, and find that the former is ten times more intense than the latter.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated ultrafast all-optical switch consisting of intersubband optical nonlinear waveguide and Michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a monolithically integrated ultrafast all-optical switch consisting of intersubband optical nonlinear waveguide in InGaAs/AlAsSb quantum wells and a Michelson interferometer. A full switching is achieved by 3 pJ control pulse energy.

articleTitle: Observation of the relativistic response of an electron-hole plasma in graphene on femtosecond timescales
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Visible pump-probe spectroscopy isolates the femtosecond Drude response of a photo generated electron-hole plasma in monolayer graphene. The observed VN scaling versus carrier density reveals the relativistic nature of the electron-hole plasma.

articleTitle: Selective gas sensing for photonic crystal lasers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We facilitate photonic crystal lasers to sense gases via an additional swelling polymer film. We describe the transduction transfer function and experimentally demonstrate an enhanced ethanol vapor sensitivity over 15 dB with low humidity crosstalk.

articleTitle: Quaternary one-dimensional photonic crystal cladding hollow-core Bragg fiber
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We proposed and fabricated hollow-core Bragg fiber with quaternary one-dimensional photonic crystal cladding. The new cladding increases the design flexibility. The transmission measurements revealed that it guides light mainly by the higher order photonic bandgaps.

articleTitle: Temporal coupled-mode theory for resonant apertures
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We develop the coupled-mode theory for resonant apertures. We show that the maximum transmission and absorption cross sections for resonant apertures are only related to the wavelength and the directivity of the aperture's radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Room temperature GaAs/AlGaAs quantum cascade lasers with InGaP and InAlP waveguides
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report the development of high temperature pulsed GaAs/AlGaAs quantum cascade lasers emitting in the wavelength range of 9 μm with threshold current density as low as 4.3 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 300K.

articleTitle: Locally-oxidized silicon surface-plasmon Schottky detector for telecom wavelengths
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate an integrated on-chip locally-oxidized silicon surface-plasmon Schottky detector for telecom wavelengths based on the internal photoemission process. Theoretical model and experimental results will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Pairwise concurrence dynamics of a 4 qubit model beyond rotating wave approximation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We examine the entanglement dynamics of two two-level systems (A & B) each interacting with separate harmonic oscillators (a & b) in a regime where rotating wave approximation is not valid.

articleTitle: A new technique to measure loss, effective refractive index and electric field distribution of THz porous fibers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We developed a new technique, employing a probe-tip, to measure both α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> and n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> of porous fibers. Moreover, using this approach, we measure the evanescent electric field as a function of frequency.

articleTitle: An integrated, noninvasive, fiber optic sensor for electric and magnetic field measurement applications
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We describe a ruggedized, nonmetallic, fiber optic sensor utilizing nonlinear crystals for measurements of electric and magnetic fields. Extensive field test results in a variety of RF sources (from dc to 20 GHz) are reported.

articleTitle: Second-order coherence of supercontinuum
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Using second-order coherence theory of nonstationary light we show that supercontinuum can be split into quasi-coherent and quasi-stationary parts. Our results opens the route for a universal definition of the coherence degree for broadband sources.

articleTitle: Compact and portable terahertz source by mixing two frequencies generated simultaneously by single solid-state laser
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: By mixing two frequencies generated from a single Q-switched Nd:YLF laser in a GaSe crystal, an average terahertz output power reaches 1 μW within a bandwidth of 65 GHz at 1.64 THz.

articleTitle: Photonic-assisted instantaneous frequency measurement based on a single Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A novel configuration with only one Mach-Zenhder interferometer for photonic-assisted instantaneous microwave frequency measurement has been proposed. A proof-of-concept experiment from 5 to 10GHz is performed, and the measurement errors almost less than 0.2GHz is successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy of Ni-Ti alloy thin films
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Using THz spectroscopy, we obtained the resistivity of Ni-Ti alloy thin-films as a function of Ti concentration. The resistivity sharply increases near the phase transition boundaries, Ti concentrations of 22%, 44% and 62%.

articleTitle: Accelerating light beams along arbitrary trajectories
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate theoretically and experimentally non-broadening optical beams that propagate along any arbitrarily-chosen convex trajectory in space. We present a general method to construct these beams and explore their universal properties using catastrophe theory.

articleTitle: An easy road to High NOON
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: ‘High-NOON’ states were generated by multiphoton interference of ‘quantum’ down-converted light with a ‘classical’ coherent state. Super-resolving phase measurements with up to five entangled photons were demonstrated with a visibility higher than obtainable without entanglement.

articleTitle: Lasers in Electronic Warfare
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The use of lasers for Electronic Warfare applications will be discussed and reviewed. Specific examples of deployed EW systems which include lasers will be presented along with a discussion of their most salient features.

articleTitle: Simultaneous clock recovery and polarization de-multiplexing for 160-Gbit/s PolM-NRZ-DQPSK using electro-optical phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A clock recovery scheme simultaneous providing polarization de-multiplexing is proposed and demonstrated in a 160-Gbit/s polarization multiplexed NRZ-DQPSK system by employing optical domain frequency down-conversion with standard RF devices.

articleTitle: Near-UV LEDs on sapphire using single crystal AlN-buffer
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: UV-LEDs were fabricated on GaN formed on sapphire using high-temperature-grown AlN buffer. For flip-chip devices, peak wavelength, output power, operation voltage and external quantum efficiency at 20 mA were 383 nm, 23 mW, 3.5 V and 36%, respectively. The internal quantum efficiency was estimated to be as high as 72%. These values were comparable to those for visible LEDs.

articleTitle: Near-omni-directional sub-micron silica light-trapping monolayer for amorphous Si photovoltaic devices
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The non-closely packed (surface-coverage of 55-65%) sub-micron silica sphere (400 nm) light-trapping monolayer was introduced to boost photocurrent (efficiency) of thin film amorphous solar cells by 15% (6.9%). The enhancement is nearly omni-directional.

articleTitle: Security of post-selection based continuous variable quantum key distribution against arbitrary attacks
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We analyse the security and performance of a continuous variable quantum key distribution protocol using post selection, deriving results that are unconditionally secure in the sense of no longer restricting the eavesdroppers attack.

articleTitle: Characterization of a difference-frequency based mid-infrared comb source
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We characterize a broad bandwidth mid-IR comb source generated through difference frequency mixing of a Yb femtosecond fiber laser. The relationship between amplitude noise, timing jitter, and output power is explored.

articleTitle: Dressing plasmons in particle-in-cavity architectures
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Metallic nanoparticles inside metal cavities show extremely strong plasmonic field enhancement both theoretically and experimentally. Plasmonic coupling gives a universal power law dependence on particle-surface gap, both for field enhancement and resonant wavelength shift.

articleTitle: Monochromatic organic photodiodes made by stackable ink-jet fabrication for integrated laser chips
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Organic photodiodes were made by ink-jet method based on the J-aggregated cyanine dye films. The radiation sensitivity and spectral resolution were improved significantly by approaches, indicating the realization of integrated flow-cytometry chips.

articleTitle: Femtosecond excitation of confined acoustic modes in 2-D arrayed GaN nanorods
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We successfully excited confined acoustic oscillations, which reflect the mechanical properties, in 2-D arrayed GaN nanorods with different diameters, by using femtosecond lasers. A nano-softening effect was observed when rod diameter was less than 150nm.

articleTitle: Dynamics of photo-excited carriers in gallium nitride under subpicosecond laser pulse excitation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present a study of subpicosecond kinetics of photo-excited carriers in bulk gallium nitride. The theoretical results are compared with the experimental results of the time-resolved photoluminescence induced by a 100-femtosecond pulse.

articleTitle: Probing quantum dot cores, their interfaces and thiol cappings non-destructively in dilute solution using Raman scattering in hollow core photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Efficient Raman scattering of thiol-capped CdTe quantum dot solutions were obtained using HC-PCF. Strong Raman modes of the CdTe core, thiol agents, and their interfacial compound were observed and compared for the first time.

articleTitle: The first ghost image using sun as a light source
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: This article reports first experimental demonstration on two-photon ghost imaging using the sun as a light source. This experimental results raises a fundamentally important question about whether the nonlocal ghost-imaging effect of classical thermal light is caused by quantum-mechanical two-photon interference. Ghost imaging using the Sun as a light source could also achieve spatial resolution equivalent to that of a classical imaging system taking pictures at a distance of 10km with a 92m-diameter lens.

articleTitle: Hollow-core-waveguides using adiabatically chirped high-contrast-gratings for a >10× loss reduction
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Chirped high-contrast-grating hollow-core waveguide demonstrates a >;10× loss reduction. Simulation shows that a propagation loss as low as 0.04 dB/cm can be achieved with a nonlinear coefficient on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> /W/m.

articleTitle: Large strain-induced conductivity anisotropy in VO2 thin films probed by THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We probe the temperature dependent far-infrared conductivity of highly strained (100)VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin films using THz TDS. A large in-plane anisotropy is observed in both the metallic conductivity and the metal-insulator transition temperature.

articleTitle: 50-MW, 12-ps Nd:YVO4 slab amplifier for OPCPA pumping
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate 12-ps pulses with 50-MW peak power from a Nd: YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> slab amplifier. The amplifier is seeded at repetition rates of 50 kHz and 100 kHz and provides output energies of up to 600 μJ.

articleTitle: Hybrid-integrated and polarization insensitive 25-Gbaud/s D(Q)PSK receiver based on polymer PLC
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a DPSK receiver with a 2×25 GHz photodiode array hybrid-integrated on polymer PLC via 45° mirrors. With a half-wave plate and micro-heaters, the polarization-dependent frequency-shift of the delay-line interferometer can be eliminated.

articleTitle: Validation of a model of a resonant optothermoacoustic trace gas sensor
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A model for a resonant optothermoacoustic sensor is validated by comparison with experiments performed with 0.5% acetylene in nitrogen. At low concentrations, the molecular dynamics of the trace gas do not influence the signal.

articleTitle: Spectral narrowing and manipulation in optical parametric oscillator using APPLN electro-optic polarization-mode converter
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report a unique spectral narrowing and manipulation technique in a PPLN optical parametric oscillator (OPO) using an APPLN electro-optic polarization-mode converter. Single to multiple spectral-narrowed and intensity-enhanced signal peaks were produced from this OPO.

articleTitle: Generation of high-power infrared laser pulses by dual-chirped optical parametric amplification scheme
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A dual-chirped optical parametric amplification scheme for generating ultrafast high-power IR pulse is proposed. Using this scheme, we can expect the generation of TW-class IR pulses in 1~2 μm.

articleTitle: Resonant in-situ photoluminescence of Si-QDs buried in SiOx/SiNx distributed Bragg reflector
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A 20-pair SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/SiN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>:Si-QDs distributed Bragg reflector with in-situ Si-QDs contributed photoluminescence at 667 nm is demonstrated to shrink the Si-QDs emission linewidth from 140 to 19 nm and enhance its intensity by 37.4 times.

articleTitle: Optical tachyons, broken PT-symmetry, and strain effects in photonic graphene
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate that optical tachyons, particles that travel faster than the speed of light can be generated by PT-symmetry breaking in photonic graphene. We further show that the PT-symmetry can be restored via strain.

articleTitle: Methods towards achieving precise birefringent focusing
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present two independent schemes for the precise focusing of orthogonal polarizations of light at arbitrary relative locations. The first scheme uses a polarization Sagnac interferometer, the second a set of three birefringent elements.

articleTitle: A distributed sensing system based on low-index Bragg reflective fiber gratings
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A sensing scheme based on fiber low-index Bragg gratings is proposed, which utilizes tunable laser to demodulate the wavelength signal. Related experiment is done to investigate.

articleTitle: Crosstalk-induced OSNR penalty prediction on 112 Gb/s PolMux-QPSK system
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Penalties from in-band crosstalk for 112 Gb/s PolMux-QPSK systems are shown to be readily determined by use of a spectrally weighted crosstalk. Experimental results demonstrate that the method is robust for linear and nonlinear regimes.

articleTitle: Modulation instability of continuous wave optical parametric oscillators
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Optical parametric oscillators exhibit a temporal modulation instability which can prevent single-longitudinal-mode operation above a certain pumping ratio. We analyze this instability and show how it can be suppressed with an intracavity etalon.

articleTitle: Interferometry with Vacuum-amplified waveforms
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Coexisting four-wave-mixing processes are observed via atomic coherence. The controllable phase and interference between these vacuum-amplified radiations look promising for applications including waveform-shaping and high-resolution metrology.

articleTitle: Fiber laser CPA system delivering 120 μJ femtosecond pulses using coherent combining
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report on the coherent combination of two chirped pulsed fiber amplifiers using a polarization cube. Femtosecond pulses were combined with an efficiency of 91% obtaining a combined pulse energy of 120 μJ.

articleTitle: Electrically pumped subwavelength metallo-dielectric laser with low threshold gain
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: An electrically pumped subwavelength metallo-dielectric laser with a low threshold gain is demonstrated. To achieve low threshold gain, we selectively etch InP electrical channel diameter. Lasing operation is observed for temperatures up to 180 K.

articleTitle: Toward flexible wafer-size 3D photonic crystal templates fabricated by scanning holographic lithography
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Parallel linear scanning laser exposure of diffractive optical elements is engineered to produce seamless stitching of thick 3D photonic crystal templates over large area and offer bandgap tuning, chirping, apodization and optofluidic integration.

articleTitle: Suppression and control over the decay of a leaky mode through a transverse refractive index gradient
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate that the decay of leaky modes can be reduced by orders of magnitude, and controlled in a robust fashion, using a transverse refractive index gradient.

articleTitle: Four-wave mixing in short silicon slow-light engineered photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report FWM (−9dB conversion) in a short (80μm) silicon dispersion engineered slow (c/30) light photonic crystal waveguide through launching a pulsed pump and a CW probe signal.

articleTitle: Widely tunable narrow-band terahertz-wave source pumped by injection-seeded optical parametric generation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We proposed a novel widely tunable terahertz-wave source pumped by injection-seeded KTP optical parametric generator. Efficient narrowing of line-width and high output of the pump source were obtained to 50 GHz and 273 μJ respectively.

articleTitle: Interferometric measurement of refractive index difference applied to composite waveguide lasers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A sensitive technique has been implemented to measure the differences in refractive indices between rare-earth doped YAG and un-doped YAG. Theoretically, a refractive index difference of less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> can be identified.

articleTitle: Preparation and local manipulation of photonic W states using expansion and fusion gates
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report experimental demonstration of an optical gate that increases the size of polarization-entangled W-states by accessing only one qubit, and discuss strategies of local expansion and fusion to prepare large scale W-state networks.

articleTitle: Beyond diffraction limited imaging and sensing in nanobiophotonics
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Based on simple fiber-optic approaches, we present some advanced nanobiophotonics methods for ultrahigh-resolution bioimaging and biosensing beyond the diffraction barrier in the subwavelength nanometric range at cellular, intracellular and bulk tissue level.

articleTitle: Shunt detection and performance characterization of silicon solar cells using thermoreflectance imaging
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Thermoreflectance is quantitatively compared with lock-in IR thermography for NDE of solar cells. The order of magnitude enhancement in spatial resolution enables shunt detection as well as extraction of local IV curves, diode parameters, and thermal diffusivity and conductivity.

articleTitle: Surface tension reshaped lithium niobate whispering gallery mode micro-resonators
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Lithium niobate micro-resonators have been fabricated by surface tension reshaping of micro-structured crystals at temperatures close to the melting point. We present preliminary results on the optical characterization of these structures.

articleTitle: The reduction of laser damage resistance of optical coatings to subpicosecond pulse trains under vacuum
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Optical multilayer materials HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> exhibit subpicosecond laser damage thresholds of just 10% of their intrinsic value when tested in vacuum. A few Torr of water vapor is shown to remedy this effect.

articleTitle: Two-photon correlations of broadband four wave mixing
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the precise time-energy correlation of light generated by ultrabroad four-waves mixing in a photonic crystal fiber. Ultra broadband sum-frequency generation serves as an ultrafast detector of both the time and frequency correlation.

articleTitle: Impact of the vertical layer structure on the emission directionality of thin-film InGaN photonic crystal LEDs
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: This work explores the impact of cavity thickness, photonic crystal etch depth, and quantum well placement on the extraction efficiency and emission directionality of thin-film InGaN photonic crystal light-emitting diodes (LEDs).

articleTitle: Plasmon resonance induced enhancement of reflection band in a one-dimensional metal nanocomposite photonic crystal
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A one-dimensional metal nanocomposite-dielectric photonic crystal that shows 200% enhancement of the reflection band due to the interplay between the plasmon resonance of the silver nanoparticles and Bloch modes of the photonic crystal is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Giant photoconductivity gain in nanowire photodetectors and the effect of photo-modulation of contact injection
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate large photoconductive gain on single-crystalline Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanowire photodetectors. The photoconductive gain is found to be significantly enhanced by optical modulation of the electrical contacts, which accounts for >;90% of the conductivity change.

articleTitle: Pump-probe melanoma imaging: Applications to high-resolution and in-vivo microscopy
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Pump-probe imaging of melanin with near-infrared pulses has been extended to two new domains: high-resolution imaging of the melanin content of melanosomes in an individual melanocyte and epi-detected in vivo microscopy of a developing melanoma.

articleTitle: LED-based CO2 sensor for balloon deployment
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We are developing a sensor for monitoring ambient CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> from unmanned aircraft and balloons. The sensor consists of a mid-IR LED coupled with a high dynamic range gated integrator. The measurement precision is 0.4 ppmv at 30 seconds.

articleTitle: Distinguishing instantaneous from rotational Kerr response in air using supercontinuum spectral interferometry
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We measure the polarization dependence of the Kerr effect in air using single-shot supercontinuum spectral interferometry, enabling separation of the instantaneous and rotational components of the nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Experimental performance of a continuously tunable 40-GHz complex weight optical FIR filter using wavelength conversion and chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a tunable and reconfigurable optical complex weight finite impulse response filter using conversion dispersion based delays with optical multicasting and multiplexing. Tuning capabilities of the filter tap amplitudes (0-10 dB), phases (0-2π) and free spectral rage (~27 and 40 GHz) are experimentally demonstrated showing close agreement with theory.

articleTitle: Microscopic study of carrier multiplication in graphene
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Microscopic calculations allow to track the ultrafast relaxation of optically excited charge carriers in graphene. Its unique band structure accounts for efficient Auger-type scattering channels resulting in a significant carrier multiplication.

articleTitle: Broadband wavelength conversion of incoherent light in silicon nanowaveguides
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate broadband wavelength conversion of an incoherent light source via four-wave mixing in a silicon rib nanowaveguide. We observe a conversion efficiency of -24 dB over the entire wavelength range of the incoherent source.

articleTitle: Silica nano-waveguides and networks as stretches on segmented organics preformed for sub-wavelength photonics
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report an original approach based on a nano-fluidic mechanism involving silica nano-particules that allowed us to design the formation of specific silica nano-patterns or organized networks of silica nano-ridges that present sub-lambda propagation regime.

articleTitle: Recent progress in quantum teleportation experiments
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Quantum teleportation is central to quantum communication, and plays an important role in a number of quantum computation protocols. In this talk, I will give a review about recent experimental progress about quantum teleportation.

articleTitle: Super-resolution via enhanced evanescent tunneling
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We propose the concept of enhanced evanescent tunneling. We show that this process can be used to probe both the amplitude and phase of the evanescent portion of the angular spectrum, thereby allowing target superresolution.

articleTitle: Lasing in metal-coated GaN nano-stripe at room temperature
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrated lasing in a metal-coated GaN nano-stripe under room temperature pulsed operation, and the lasing mode at 370nm were observed. Aluminum and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layers were coated on the undoped GaN nano-stripe.

articleTitle: Three-photon counting in a photomultiplier tube for ultrafast source characterization
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally ultrafast three-photon counting by three-photon absorption in a photomultiplier tube, which may serve as a unique tool for ultrafast quantum state characterization as well as for ultrasensitive temporal measurements.

articleTitle: Low-loss hollow metallic waveguides efficiently coupled to terahertz micro-ring quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate that the azimuthally polarized beam of a micro-ring THz quantum cascade laser can be coupled to hollow metallic waveguides with efficiencies ≥96% and perfectly matched with the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> waveguide mode, giving attenuation losses <;3dB/m.

articleTitle: Temporal contrast improvement of femtosecond pulses by a self-diffraction process in a Kerr bulk medium
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We improved the temporal contrast of a femtosecond pulse by more than four orders magnitude of its incident pulse using self-diffraction process in a 0.5-mm-thick glass plate. The energy transform efficiency is about 12%.

articleTitle: Passively carrier-envelope phase stable mid-IR OPCPA source at 100 kHz repetition rate
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present a carrier-envelope stable, 100 kHz source of intense 6 cycle mid-IR pulses at 3.2 microns. The CEP stability is sub-100 mrad RMS over 1 million pulses.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of closed mode Q-factor in terahertz metamaterial superlattice
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Terahertz metamaterial superlattice is fabricated with double-split ring resonators. By cooling down to the cryogenic temperature 4K, changes in Q-factor of closed mode resonance originating from coherent coupling in metamaterial are investigated.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of a THz quantum cascade laser using a dual fs-fiber laser comb technique
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Electro-optic sampling in ZnTe is used to phase-lock the line of a 2.5 THz quantum cascade laser to the repetition rate of a femtosecond fibre laser and to perform an absolute measurement of the laser emission frequency.

articleTitle: All-optical logic gates (NAND and AND) based on multi-injection in single mode Fabry-Perot Laser
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: All-optical NAND and AND gate using single mode Fabry-Perot Laser diode (SMFP LD) is demonstrated. The operating principle is based on the intensity modulation of SMFP-LD with combined input power of the logic gates.

articleTitle: Long path (167 m) broad-band THz transmission through the atmosphere
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We have transmitted a low-power beam of repetitive broad-band THz pulses the record distance of 167 m through the atmosphere at 50% relative humidity and have observed the broadened transmitted pulses with a signal to noise ratio greater than 200.

articleTitle: Scale-free optics and diffractionless waves in nano-disordered ferroelectrics
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: In supercooled nanodisordered KLTN we report light propagation where wavelength is cancelled by nonlinearity. Diffraction is not compensated, but ceases: beams form solitons of any size and intensity, even arbitrarily low, allowing ultraresolved imaging microscopy.

articleTitle: Enhancement of two photon processes in quantum dots embedded in subwavelength metallic gratings
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A 20-fold enhancement of two-photon absorption and light upconversion in InAs nanocrystal quantum dots is achieved using resonant local field enhancements in subwavelength nanoslit arrays.

articleTitle: The intelligence advanced research projects activity — Its BEST and beyond
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: In October 2007, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) formally established the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA). IARPA's mission is to invest in high-risk/high-payoff research programs that have the potential to provide the U.S. with an overwhelming intelligence advantage over our future adversaries. Biometrics has surfaced as a technology area of interest to IARPA. Today's biometric acquisition systems generally require cooperative or conditioned individuals under controlled or constrained conditions to achieve desired levels of recognition performance. IARPA's Office of Smart Collection has established the Biometrics Exploitation Science and Technology (BEST) Program to significantly: 1) advance the Intelligence Community's (IC) ability to achieve high-confidence match performance, even when the features are derived from non-ideal data; and 2) relax the constraints currently required to acquire high fidelity biometric signatures. The BEST Program is addressing many of the underlying biometrics technology challenges by investigating innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, algorithms, devices, and systems. IARPA is also seeking innovative ideas and concepts for the advancement of standoff biometrics technologies. IARPA's mission is to invest in high-risk/high-payoff research programs that have the potential to provide the U.S. with an overwhelming intelligence advantage over our future adversaries. Biometrics has surfaced as a technology area of interest to IARPA. Today's biometric acquisition systems generally require cooperative or conditioned individuals under controlled or constrained conditions to achieve desired levels of recognition performance. IARPA's Office of Smart Collection has established the Biometrics Exploitation Science and Technology (BEST) Program to significantly: 1) advance the Intelligence Community's (IC) ability to achieve high-confidence match performance, even when the features are derived from non-ideal data; and 2) relax the constraints currently required to acquire high fidelity biometric signatures. The BEST Program is addressing many of the underlying biometrics technology challenges by investigating innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, algorithms, devices, and systems. IARPA is also seeking innovative ideas and concepts for the advancement of standoff biometrics technologies. An emphasis is placed on classifying and recognizing unique human phenomenology (i.e. anatomical, physiological, and/or behavioral), or novel biometric signatures, that may by acquired from significantly greater ranges than from today's commercially available biometrics technology.l, and/or behavioral), or novel biometric signatures, that may by acquired from significantly greater ranges than from today's commercially available biometrics technology.

articleTitle: Incident field image reconstruction using speckle intensity correlations over position
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Speckle images are used to form speckle intensity spatial correlations over incident light position. These correlations allow the reconstruction of the field incident on and transmitted through a heavily scattering medium.

articleTitle: Real-time self-homodyne coherent receiver for BPSK signals using feed-forward carrier extraction
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate the first real-time self-homodyne coherent receiver for 10.66Gbit/s BPSK signals using an OEO based carrier extraction scheme without using any pilot tone.

articleTitle: Controlled spatiotemporal focusing through turbid media
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We apply adaptive beam shaping for spatiotemporal focusing of ultrashort pulses through turbid media, in the context of nonlinear microscopy. We find that controlled temporal shaping is attainable using only the spatial degrees of control.

articleTitle: Interaction of strong terahertz pulses with exciton-polaritons in quantum-well microcavity
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Interaction of strong THz pulses with a QW microcavity reveals that exciton-polariton modes and 2p-exciton state form a Λ-type three-level system. THz pulses resonantly drive the transitions from the exciton-polariton states to the 2p-exciton state.

articleTitle: On the optimal choice of states for process tomography
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Quantum process tomography requires a set of input states sensitive to the unknown process. We experimentally generate a class of 4-photon states and compare their sensitivity to that of coherent states to a decohering process.

articleTitle: High power III-Nitride UV emitters
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Increasing power and efficiency of UV semiconductor light sources enables great expansion of system applications. We review state-of-the-art III-Nitride LEDs and report on improved device designs and fabrication for achieving high power operation.

articleTitle: Characterization of a high-contrast front-end prototype for the OMEGA EP laser facility
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The temporal and spectral properties of a high-contrast front-end prototype developed for the OMEGA EP chirped pulse amplification system are described. A hundredfold contrast improvement and improved beam quality are obtained.

articleTitle: Tracking charge transfer in carbon nanotube networks with chirped pump-probe spectroscopy
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We observed an ultrafast charge generation and transfer in a carbon nanotube network by a novel pump-probe spectroscopy that makes use of a broadband and positively chirped pump and transform-limited probe pulses.

articleTitle: Conical intersection dynamics in a Rhodopsin analog: 9-cis Isorhodopsin
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Using broadband sub-20-fs ultrafast spectroscopy we study the conical intersection dynamics in the visual pigment analog 9-cis Isorhodopsin. We find a longer excited state lifetime and oscillations suggestive of pulsed photoproduct formation.

articleTitle: High-energy gain-switched mid-IR lasers based on Cr and Fe doped ZnSe
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report an optimization of transition-metal (Cr and Fe) doped ZnSe crystals fabrication and energy scaling of gain-switched Cr:ZnSe (10mJ@2.4μm) and Fe:ZnSe (3.6mJ@4.37μm) lasers operating at 300K.

articleTitle: Fast swept-source generation based on fiber optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a fast frequency swept-source using the dispersive Fourier transformation-based fiber optical parametric amplifier. The swept rate is as high as 78 MHz, with a linewidth of 0.135 nm.

articleTitle: Cold atoms coupled to a superconducting flux qubit
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present a scheme and our advances to magnetically couple Rb atoms to a superconducting flux qubit by trapping the atoms in the evanescent wave outside an tapered optical fiber.

articleTitle: Synchronously pumped tunable Raman laser in the visible pumped by an all-fiber PM MOPA at 1060 nm
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report a pulsed, visible Raman laser synchronously pumped by the frequency doubled output of an all-fiber MOPA at 1060nm. Almost 2.3THz continuous tuning was achieved for individual Stokes order spanning from green to orange.

articleTitle: Ultracompact wavelength-selective silicon-based plasmonic components
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: High performance of a ring resonator and add-drop multiplexer with extremely small ring radius (1 or 2 μm) and a sub-wavelength confinement area of λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/1200 is reported. It has been achieved using the silicon-based hybrid dielectric-loaded plasmonic waveguide approach.

articleTitle: Sub-15 nm photo-electron source using a nano-aperture integrated with a nano-antenna
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We propose a nano-scale C-aperture nano-tip photo-electron source with a CsBr photo cathode. We fabricated the structure and estimated the optical spot available in the CsBr thin film with photoresist exposure.

articleTitle: Towards a real-time electro-optical THz microscope using a demodulating optical detector array
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present an electro-optical THz microscope with parallel readout of 3072 pixels. The use of a demodulating detector array increases the efficiency of the setup enabling the use of a non-amplified fs-laser for electro-optic detection.

articleTitle: Observation of Glauber-Fock dynamics in photonic lattices
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report the first observation of classical intensity distributions in optical arrays that are totally analogous to quantum coherent and displaced Fock states. Bloch-like oscillations and revivals are also predicted in such Glauber-Fock photonic lattices.

articleTitle: On-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report the first demonstration of on-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS). The measured Brillouin shift and line width are ~7.7 GHz and 6 MHz in a 7 cm long chalcogenide waveguide.

articleTitle: Room-temperature, high-efficiency conversion of Mott-Wannier excitons to Frenkel excitons in hybrid semiconductor quantum dot/polymer composites
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Efficient conversion from Mott-Wannier to Frenkel excitons at room temperature is observed in hybrid inorganic/organic composites of CdSe/ZnS core/shell heteronanocrystals in MDMO-PPV homopolymers at a rate of 0.2628 ns<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with an efficiency of 80.9%.

articleTitle: Experimental security analysis a four-photon private state
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report experimental generation of a noisy entangled four-photon state that exhibits a separation between secure key contents and distillable entanglement. This difference is exposed by a detailed analysis of its privacy properties.

articleTitle: Combining angle-resolved Raman scattering and confocal Raman microscopy for rationally designing two-dimensional metallic arrays as high performing SERS substrates
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We study the dependence of surface-enhanced Raman scattering from metallic arrays on geometry by angle-resolved Raman spectroscopy and confocal microscopy. It is found that both Raman profile and intensity are strongly dependent on hole size.

articleTitle: Chemically-specific photoacoustic imaging using vibrational Raman excitation
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate, for the first time, molecular contrast imaging in deep tissue by successfully combining chemically-selective, stimulated Raman photoexcitation with high-frequency ultrasound detection.

articleTitle: Helically propagating modes in InGaAs nanoneedle lasers grown on poly-silicon and silicon substrates
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: InGaAs nanoneedle lasers were grown on both poly crystalline-Si and (100)-Si substrates by low temperature (400°C) MOCVD. Measured near field mode patterns agree well with FDTD simulations, confirming helically propagating modes as lasing modes.

articleTitle: True bulk GaN technology for high efficiency devices
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: As GaN device technologies confront the need to increase yield and performance metrics, expected material improvements will come from the use of lattice-matched substrates. There is a growing interest in utilizing low-defect density GaN substrates for certain high performance applications. Manufacturers who make use of true bulk substrates will have the first opportunity to achieve the theoretically predicted performance and reliability for GaN-based devices. This paper will outline the progress of bulk GaN crystal growth techniques, and compare their various merits and deficiencies. Solvothermal growth, flux growth, and vapor phase growth are the main contenders that must prove their ability to provide high quality material consistently and at a competitive price. To validate their claims, we will discuss issues such as wafer purity, defect density, lattice bending, growth rate, and reproducibility.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon resonances in silver Bowtie nanoantennas with varied bow angles
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Numerical simulations and experimental measurements to plasmon resonances in Ag Bowtie nanoantennas show that, as the bow angle increases, one fundamental resonance blue- and then red-shifts; two types of high-order resonances emerge at large angles.

articleTitle: Nd:YVO4 laser mode-locking at 1.34 μm by negative χ(2)-lens formation in an intracavity BIBO crystal
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Self-starting χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>-lens mode-locking of a 1.34-μm Nd:YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> laser using second harmonic generation in BiB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is demonstrated. Pulses as short as 3.7 ps and average powers reaching 1.3 W at 120 MHz are achieved.

articleTitle: Impact of the maritime environment on the aging of optical fibers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The effect of the maritime environment on the aging of optical fibers coatings was studied. The obtained stress decay rate was 29.05 days, however, this value is higher than for a pure water saturate environment.

articleTitle: Coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) holographic biological imaging
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate non-scanning three-dimensional (3D) imaging of cellular components in live cancerous (HeLa) cells by combining the chemical selectivity of CARS with the 3D imaging capability of holography to establish a new technique for bio-imaging.

articleTitle: Light-matter strong coupling in the mid-infrared region with metallic microcavities
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a very strong coupling between a mid-infrared intersubband excitation of a two-dimensional electron gas and a microcavity mode, obtained thanks to a sub-wavelength confinement of the light between two metal layers.

articleTitle: Simultaneous oxygenation and flow using current modulation of VCSELs during ischemia
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: In this work we demonstrate simultaneous laser speckle contrast imaging and multispectral reflectance imaging with coherence modulated VCSEL illumination during cortical ischemia. The advantages of VCSELs for potable hemodynamic monitoring are discussed.

articleTitle: Quasiprobability representations of quantumness
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Quasiprobability representations of quantumness are developed, including entanglement and space-time dependent field correlation properties. General quantum effects are visualized by negativities of regular functions accessible in experiments.

articleTitle: Optomechanically-coupled fishbone-shaped double-beam nanoresonators
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate gradient-force-induced mechanical oscillations in optomechanically-coupled fishbone-shaped double-beam nanocavities. Details in design, fabrication, and measurement will be discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical investigations on Kerr-induced long-period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We numerically analyze broadband (up to 60 nm) conversion of transverse modes with long-period fiber gratings that are transiently introduced via the optical Kerr effect.

articleTitle: New generation of distributed Bragg reflectors based on BAlN/AlN structures for deep UV-optoelectronic applications
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report innovative highly reflective DBR structures based on the novel material BAlN. An experimental BAlN/AlN DBRs demonstrated a reflectivity of 60% and 82% at wavelengths of 282 nm and 311nm respectively.

articleTitle: CH fluorescence imaging at high repetition rates
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We introduce a novel strategy to acquire CH PLIF images at high repetition rates. A multi-mode pumped optical parametric oscillator (OPO) which produces signal at 431 nm is used for direct excitation of the CH radical.

articleTitle: Interaction between metamaterial resonators and inter-subband transitions in quantum wells
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Interaction between metamaterial elements and intersubband transitions in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells is observed in the mid-infrared. Transmission measurements were performed through metamaterial arrays, each having a different resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Cavity optomechanics — A tutorial introduction
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A collection of slides from the author's presentation, regarding quantum metrology, quantum limit, radiation pressure mirror cooling, quantum mechanics and ground states.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband chirp linearity characterization with an optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The linearity of actively stabilized laser chirp from approximately 1530 to 1570 nm is measured by use of an optical frequency comb showing residuals of <; 60 kHz after removing low order dispersion related effects.

articleTitle: Decay time in a cavity in slow or fast light regime
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We investigate the decay time of a cavity containing strong dispersion achieved through EIT in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>He* with linear polarizations. The photon lifetime is shown to be governed by the group velocity of light.

articleTitle: Probing of multi component gas samples by means of supercontinuum CRD-spectrography
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The ring-down decay inside a high optical bandwidth cavity was excited by using the white light supercontinuum emitted from a photonic fiber to determine absorption properties of atmospheric air between 610-730 nm by means of the CRD-Spectrography.

articleTitle: Noise performance of time stretch system with distributed and discrete amplifiers
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We analyzed the noise performance of time stretched analog to digital converter with both lumped and distributed amplification cases. We show that distributed amplification provides up to 16dB higher SNR corresponding to ~2.5 bit higher resolution.

articleTitle: Interference of two photons of different color with applications to quantum computing
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Two photons having different colors can undergo the Hong-Ou-Mandel interference effect if the usual beam splitter is replaced by Bragg scattering via four-wave mixing in an optical fiber, which acts as a frequency shifter.

articleTitle: High-fidelity frontend based on XPW filter for high-contrast few-cycle OPCPAs
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate a 80μJ, 5fs, CEP-stable injector with high spectro-temporal quality. The device relies on post-compression in a hollow-core fiber followed by XPW filtering and is an ideal seed for high-power high-contrast OPCPA systems.

articleTitle: Tokyo QKD Network and the evolution to Secure Photonic Network
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A novel secure communication network with quantum key distribution in a metropolitan area is reported. Different QKD schemes are integrated to demonstrate secure TV conferencing over a distance 45km, stable long-term operation, and application to secure mobile phones.

articleTitle: Agenda of sessions — Sunday, 1 May
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: Ultrafast lattice dynamics in fs laser-excited FeRh probed by time-resolved X-ray diffraction
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Time-resolved X-ray diffraction with ultrashort X-ray pulses from a laser-produced plasma is used to study the lattice response of a thin FeRh-film during a fs laser-driven anti-ferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase transition.

articleTitle: Fiber Fabry-Pérot laser mode-locked by graphene for the generation of supercontinuum with 10GHz mode spacing
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We propose a passively mode-locked fiber laser with 9.67GHz fundamental repetition rate (10mm cavity length) using a graphene saturable absorber. Supercontinuum with 0.08nm mode spacing is generated using this laser and a highly nonlinear fiber.

articleTitle: Eigen mode approach to the sub-wavelength imaging with surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We develop a novel physically transparent model that establishes unequivocal connection between surface plasma polariton (SPP) modes and sub-wavelength imaging in the super-lens, and use it to analyze the modulation transfer function.

articleTitle: Femtosecond pulses generation from chromium-doped cunyite laser
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Femtosecond pulses as short as 365 fs were generated from a Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4+</sup>: Cunyite laser using a combination of a broadband semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM), chirped mirrors, and passive mode locking.

articleTitle: Fano resonances in reduced symmetry metamaterials
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate the Fano resonance in reduced symmetry metamaterials with both inversion symmetry being broken, and show that two bright modes of perpendicular polarizations can be hybridized by this Fano resonance. Experimental results are shown and demonstrate the onset of Fano resonances as the coupling between the bright modes and the dark mode overcome resistive losses in the metal.

articleTitle: Efficient schemes for adaptive optics in high-resolution microscopy
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Specimen-induced aberrations frequently affect image quality in high-resolution microscopes. We develop efficient adaptive optical schemes to correct aberrations in confocal, multiphoton and harmonic generation microscopes. Image resolution and contrast is improved with minimal specimen exposure.

articleTitle: Nuclear spin induced collapse and revival shape of Rabi oscillations of a single electron spin in diamond
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report Rabi beatings induced by host nitrogen nuclear spin of a single Nitrogen-Vacancy center in diamond. Different orientation of host nuclear spin leads to a triplet splitting of the transition between two spin states.

articleTitle: Motion compensation for two photon microscopy by optical coherence tomography feedback
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Active motion compensation using a Fourier-domain optical coherent tomography as a distance sensor of a two-photon microscope has been implemented. It demonstrated good feasibility and corrected the images under the sample motion in the z-direction.

articleTitle: MHz-rate high-resolution reflectometry by direct mapping of the full axial-line profile in a single-shot oscilloscope trace
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A concept is introduced for optical reflectometry based on real-time spectral interference pattern Fourier transformation, enabling direct axial-line mapping with hundreds of sampling points in a single-shot oscilloscope trace at MHz update rates.

articleTitle: Photon-phonon entanglement in a coupled optomechanical system
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We consider two coupled optomechanical cavities exploring entanglement between all modes in the collective system. In addition to intra cavity entanglement [1], interestingly we find remarkably robust steady state inter cavity photon-phonon entanglement.

articleTitle: A low-cost, bandwidth-efficient Fabry-Pérot optical millimeter-wave generator driven by low RF frequencies
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Optical mm-waves are generated via a new frequency-tripling and quadrupling scheme, respectively, which is based on directly modulated optically injection locked Fabry-Perot laser. Error-free transmission of millimeter-wave signal over 20-km SSMF has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Multilayered optical storage in Sm(DBM)3Phen-doped and un-doped polymethylmethacrylate by a femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We report on multilayered optical storage in Srn(DBM)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Phen-doped and un-doped polymethylmethacrylate read out by fluorescence and reflection modes. The detection of fluorescence signal enables retrieval of the stored bits with a higher signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Au and Ag nano-particle embedded plasmonic metal-slotted polymer electro-optic waveguide modulator
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A new electro-optic (EO) plasmonic metal-slotted optical waveguide (PMOW) modulator based on gold and silver metal islandized thin films is proposed and experimentally demonstrated that can be operated at both 1310 nm and 1550 nm wavelengths. The fabricated PMOWs are also able to support both TM and TE polarizations, and their characteristics of the EO PMOW modulators are discussed.

articleTitle: Sub-300 nm UV LEDs with defect reduction layer and vertical-injection architecture
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We present UV LEDs operating at wavelengths below 300 nm. The heterostructure features a defect reduction layer that bends threading dislocations away from the active region. Vertical-injection structures were fabricated via laser lift-off.

articleTitle: Ceramic plasmonic components for optical metamaterials
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: The performance of metamaterial and transformation-optics devices is limited by losses in their plasmonic components. We show that ceramics (heavily doped-zinc oxide and titanium nitride) could help in overcoming the loss issue in the optical range.

articleTitle: Radial polarization interferometer
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: We demonstrate an interferometer based on interference of radially and azimuthally polarized beams. The spatially varying intensity provides additional information improving phase change measurements compared with a conventional interferometer.

articleTitle: Surface modified structure for photon extraction of UV-LED
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: Ultra-violet light-emitting diodes (UV-LEDs) fabricated with integrated surface textures show an enhancement of the output power and more directionality of the emitted light, which is in agreement with the calculated results.

articleTitle: Hybrid-integrated germanium photodetector and CMOS receiver operating at 15 Gb/s
publicationTitle: CLEO: 2011 - Laser Science to Photonic Applications
abstract: A waveguide-integrated metal-semiconductor-metal photodetector is integrated with an analog 90-nm CMOS receiver. Error-free 15-Gb/s operation is achieved with an efficiency of 4.7 pJ/bit and a sensitivity of -8 dBm average power.
